title: What is known about 1RB1LB_1LC0RE_0LE0LD_0LC---_1LA0RF_1RE1LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LB_1LC0RE_0LE0LD_0LC---_1LA0RF_1RE1LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The left side is a list of segments xn (x = 1110) separated by 1 0 11 0 and 00 markers. Lean proves the twelve shift rules the sweeps use; the cascade is only observed.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 31,493 cells have been visited and 16,808 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.492). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.08).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: Twelve rules over words of 2 and 4 cells, each for every n and every tape around; e.g. F turns (0111)<sup>n</sup> into (0010)<sup>n</sup> going right (12 steps a word), C turns (0010)<sup>n</sup> back into (1110)<sup>n</sup> going left.

claims.title: The walking marker
claims.text: Between steps 2.048·109 and 2.075·109 the tape is … x^a 1 0 11 0 x^b 00 x^c 1 0 11 0 x^1939 1 0 11 0 x^78 00 x^5 111 with b falling by about 26 per visit of the left end (579 → 9) while c grows by the same (3766 → 4336) and a by about 3.5; then the marker restarts (x^5405 00 x^5 …) and the 00 marker of the last segment moves by 8 (x^78 00 x^5 → x^70 00 x^13).

claims.title: The counter on the right
claims.text: The right side gains one cell at steps 3.0·10<sup>8</sup>, 4.9·10<sup>8</sup>, 7.6·10<sup>8</sup>, 1.11·10<sup>9</sup>, 1.61·10<sup>9</sup>, 2.41·10<sup>9</sup>: each record about 1.5 times later.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open: the rule of the cascade is not proved and the halting transition (D reading 1) is not located in it.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is a list of long segments of one 4-cell word. A marker walks through one segment, carrying words across, then jumps back to the start, while a counter at the right grows by one cell every time the run gets 1.5 times older.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
Time between records of the right side.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.492). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.08).
After 109 steps the tape spans 31,493 cells (25,674 left of the start, 57 right), with a density of 1s of 0.534.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Segments and a walking marker
html: With x = 1110, the tape at step 2,048,043,645 is A>0 1 0 x^5326 1 0 11 0 x^579 00 x^3766 1 0 11 0 x^1939 1 0 11 0 x^78 00 x^5 111, with about 60 cells right of the start. At each later visit of the head to the left end, the segment before the 00 marker is about 26 words shorter and the one after it 26 longer: the marker walks left through the segment. When it arrives (x^9), it is reborn after the first segment and the marker in the last segment moves on by 8 words.
The sweeps that do this rewrite x as 0010/0111 and back; those shift rules are proved in Lean for every length.

sections.heading: Open
html: The halting transition is D reading 1. The cascade looks like a counter with several digits (the positions of the markers) plus a slow counter on the right; its rule, and the configuration that would trigger D1, have not been worked out.

summary: Segments of the word 1110 with markers between them; a 00 marker walks through a segment, moving words from one side to the other, and restarts at the far left when done, while a counter right of the start gains a cell each time the run is 1.5 times older; macro rule not proved.
family: segment cascade with a walking marker + counter (unresolved)
